highlights.title: Belkin’s first trackers come ready to attach to your gear.
highlights.summary: After selling accessories for attaching Apple's AirTags to everything from keys to backpacks, Belkin is introducing its own trackers that work with either Apple's Find My or Google's Find Hub tracking networks.
body: If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The cheapest and simplest option is the $14.99 Belkin SureFind Spot that comes tethered to a metal key ring, but for $24.99 the SureFind Loop Cable Tag comes with extra functionality in the form of a secure carry loop that doubles as a short USB-C to USB-C charging cable. Both are expected to be available sometime this month.

To keep tabs on your wallet without adding a lot of extra bulk the $26.99 SureFind Card is a credit card–sized alternative that comes with an IP68 rating. It can survive a “prolonged submersion in water” according to Belkin, but since Bluetooth doesn’t work under water you’ll have to rely on the tracker’s last known location to find it.

Belkin’s most expensive tracker is its $39.99 SureFind Wallet Stand that attaches to mobile devices with magnets, functions as a fold-out stand, and protects your payment cards from wireless snooping by blocking RFID signals. While the SureFind Card is launching this month, you’ll have to wait until October for the Wallet Stand to become available.

highlights.title: From MIT to IBM, expediting AI and quantum deployment
highlights.summary: MIT affiliates engage with the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab to bring rigorous theory to production systems.
body: The experience of transitioning from research based in theory to focusing on real-world application can vary significantly for different researchers. However, for two former MIT graduate students and a former postdoc, all now at IBM, working with the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab (formerly the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab) during their formative years enabled them to not only close the gap between education and employment, but also to generate ideas promising to business impact.

Despite pursuing varied careers in quantum machine learning, reinforcement learning and artificial intelligence agents,and trustworthy and fair AI, respectively, Srinivasan Arunachalam, Zhang-Wei Hong PhD ’25, and Irene Ko PhD ’24 have consistently found ways to tackle problems defined by novelty and rigor, and translate them to systems with real constraints. Here, the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab served as a conduit for research relationship building and the flow of their expertise to industry applications.

highlights.title: Shields or Taylor the greatest? "We're 1A and 1B!"
highlights.summary: Claressa Shields has hailed the greatness of Katie Taylor and says she holds no qualms over a fight between the boxing greats never materialising.
body: Claressa Shields and Amanda Serrano both wished Katie Taylor a happy retirement as the Irish great prepares for the final bout of her professional career this weekend; Shields played down the idea she was upset the two never shared the ring, praising Taylor's historic career.
Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans.
The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history.
Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport.

highlights.title: Following Nintendo's example, Sony and Microsoft argue they have no obligation to pass tariff refunds onto customers
highlights.summary: Lawyers representing Sony and Microsoft have argued, in two separate lawsuits, that the platform holders are not obligated to pass tariff refunds back to consumers. Sony and Microsoft have had to raise prices of their PlayStation and Xbox consoles in 2025 in response to US-imposed tariffs.
body: Both Sony and Microsoft will receive refunds, but consumers who paid higher prices for their products as a result of the tariffs will not be compensated. As reported by Game File, the two companies are being sued separately by affected consumers who say they should receive refunds.
In Sony's case, brought against it by a group of players in California, the company used a familiar line of argument that essentially said consumers got what they paid for.

"Paying fair market price for voluntarily purchased consumer goods is not a legally cognisable injury in fact," Sony argued in a legal motion. The company is seeking to dismiss the suit early before it could turn into a class-action lawsuit.
Microsoft's case was initiated by one individual in Washington State, who is likewise seeking a refund. Once again, the company's argument against the suit is familiar.

body: The agreement makes good on plans Supercell first put forward in the spring, when it said it planned to buy the remaining shares of Metacore and add Merge Mansion to its already impressive roster, which includes Hay Day and Clash of Clans. Player-facing services will resume service as normal while the acquisition process moves forward, and Metacore's development team will keep supporting the existing community. In other words, players don’t need to be worried that things may change.

highlights.title: Four Seasons Launches Refresh of Hotel Danieli
highlights.summary: Built in 1471 and converted into a hospitality destination in 1822, Danieli is always a hub of activity during the film festival: "We are inaugurating a new chapter in the history of this celebrated palazzo."
body: A gothic gem overlooking Venice’s iconic lagoon got a refresh in time for the Venice Film Festival.

French interior designer Pierre-Yves Rochon steered the renovation by focusing on a “balance of history, light and materials” per Four Seasons. The color palette is said to have been inspired by the lagoon and mixed with inspiration from Venice’s marble facades, plasterwork and architecture through the use of celadon greens, soft blues, terracotta, ochre and powder pink.

Inside the Palazzo Dandolo lobby, hand-restored gilding creates a quatrefoil motif against a blue background reminiscent of water while the columns, stonework and the staircase were restored by local artisans. The space also leans on natural light through Venetian mirrors while Murano glass, Venetian terrazzo floors and Rubelli fabrics connect each space to Venetian tradition and codes. A collection or artworks has been curated to honor Venice’s heritage and history as a destination for artists and writers.

highlights.title: You be the judge: should my girlfriend stop letting the recycling pile up?
highlights.summary: Robin keeps used packaging on the kitchen ledge. Benny thinks that’s unhygienic. You decide who’s talking rubbish. • Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror. We’ve had little flies buzzing around – I know they’re coming from the recycling.
body: My girlfriend, Robin, likes to keep the recycling on a ledge above the counter in our kitchen, instead of taking it straight outside. I absolutely hate it. It’s not just empty cereal boxes or clean bottles – we have a dog, so there are often empty dog food cans too. There’s always a bit of food left around the edges, and if they’re left for long enough they start to smell and attract flies. It’s gross.

We live in a flat on the third floor, so I understand not wanting to make a trip to the bin every time we finish something, but there has to be a limit. If the cans are growing mould or attracting flies, we’ve passed it. I don’t want to be preparing food while there’s a collection of old things sitting above the counter.

I’ve suggested rinsing the cans as soon as we’ve used them, which Robin does sometimes, but not often. We have a small kitchen and clear surfaces make it feel calmer and cleaner. Twelve pieces of recycling lined up along the wall is an eyesore.

highlights.title: Belkin introduces its first longer-lasting semi-solid-state power banks
highlights.summary: Belkin is joining companies like BMX, Kuxiu, and Zens with the launch of its first power banks featuring semi-solid-state battery technology. The company claims the new accessories have been "engineered to last up to 3x longer than other power banks" with the addition of a "gel-like layer"…
body: The company says its new power banks will last up to three times longer before they need to be replaced.

Other advantages of what Belkin is calling its BoostSolid Cell technology include a reduced risk of overheating that could cause swelling or fires and consistent power delivery across a wider temperature range. They’re more expensive than power banks with comparable specs, but a longer functional lifespan should outweigh the premium pricing.

The UltraCharge Pro Slim Magnetic Power Bank 5K Qi2 15W with BoostSolid Cell is the smaller and cheaper option of Belkin’s two new power banks at $69.99. The company claims it’s 40 percent slimmer than other 5,000mAh power banks and is designed to magnetically hang on the back of compatible mobile devices and wirelessly deliver up to 15W of power. A USB-C charging port can also be used to power other devices at up to 22.5W, but charging two devices simultaneously drops the output to just 5W wirelessly and 12W with a USB-C cable.

highlights.title: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more
highlights.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, arriving just a few weeks after its predecessor. The company claims the new model "works harder" than Gemini 3.7 Flash by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and "calling tools iteratively." It has the same introductory pricing as 3.7 Flash, $0.75 per…
body: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is also launching to Google’s new Fairwind Program.

Gemini 3.8 Flash’s launch was followed by some early impressions online. Artificial Analysis highlighted the model’s pricing, saying Gemini 3.8 Flash is “the cheapest we’ve measured at this level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations.”

Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared Gemini 3.8 Flash to Anthropic’s models, saying it offers “Opus 5 coding quality but at a fraction of the cost and super fast,” adding, “This is going to be so awesome for things like making remotion videos.”

Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash offers “significant improvements” for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. It outperforms its predecessor and other frontier models on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, including Anthropic’s Fable 5, which got an upgrade earlier this week that also promises stronger performance at a lower price, by cutting the price to use cached data.

highlights.summary: More than 60 years since their release, all three movies in Clint Eastwood’s “The Man with No Name Trilogy” remain classics. 1964’s A Fistful of Dollars, 1965’s For a Few Dollars More, and 1996’s The Good, the Bad and the Ugly are all Italian-made films by director Sergio Leone set in the American…
body: They are so successful that they overshadow Eastwood’s very next Western after completing the trilogy, a movie that is every bit as good as the Man with No Name movies. It’s also a film that's entirely free to stream on YouTube.

Hang ‘Em High is a 1968 Western directed by Ted Post, written by Leonard Freeman and Mel Goldberg, and produced by Eastwood himself. The Man with No Name movies made Eastwood a star, so he used some of that clout to begin to exercise his muscle as a filmmaker. He personally chose Post, who he worked with on the TV show Rawhide (1959), to direct, and Eastwood also made script changes to Hang ‘Em High to flesh out his character. Eastwood didn’t direct a movie himself until a few years later, but Hang ‘Em High is a milestone on his path to becoming one of America’s great directors.

highlights.summary: Our heroes travel back through time to San Francisco in 1986 so they can commune with aliens threatening future Earth – it’s preposterously good fun. Here is the fourth and silliest movie in the Star Trek franchise, now on rerelease for its 40th anniversary.
body: Spock has been brought back to life, as the apparent end result of all the bizarre metempsychotic plot contortions of the previous film. But the permanent and irrevocable death of Kirk’s son seems to be passed over remarkably casually. The eerie boyishness of Shatner’s Kirk, with that beaming smile, almost makes you forget that he has been through an agonising bereavement. Hasn’t he?

Starting today, September 3rd, if you own Nanoleaf Hexagon, Triangle, or Mini Triangle wall panels, you can integrate them into your Philips Hue ecosystem using a Philips Hue x Nanoleaf Wall Light Module. highlights.title: I camped in one of Britain’s last remaining rainforests
highlights.summary: A fragment of temperate rainforest lies on the edge of Dartmoor, and following years of conservation work, its owners have now opened up a sustainable campsite next to this fragile ecosystem.
body: Mist blankets the valley as I wheel my camping gear down the small hill towards a clearing ringed by trees and shrubs. A picnic bench sits at its edge, angled towards the reason why I’m here: one of the last remaining fragments of temperate rainforest in Britain. I’m pitching my tent at Wray Valley Camping, a low-impact site on Dartmoor’s eastern edge between Lustleigh and Moretonhampstead, where I’ll spend five days on one of the site’s “nearly wild” pitches.

Also known as Atlantic woodland, temperate rainforests depend on a rare combination of high humidity, rainfall and consistently mild coastal temperatures where the sea moderates the climate. They once stretched from the western Highlands of Scotland down to Cornwall, covering 20% of the UK, and sheltering rare and delicate lichens and plants. Today more than 95% of our temperate rainforest cover is gone, but Devon’s near-constant dampness and its exposure to the Atlantic make it one of the last strongholds for this rare habitat.
Wray Valley Camping owners Michelle Grist and her partner Kevin Chamberlain have spent seven years restoring this fragile ecosystem while developing the adjacent campsite.

highlights.title: Trump Administration Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Lawsuit
highlights.summary: The US government wrote a letter in support of OpenAI’s argument that training AI on others' intellectual property is fair use.
body: The Trump Administration just took OpenAI’s side in the artificial intelligence company’s legal battle with the New York Times.

The media juggernaut sued OpenAI and Microsoft in 2023, alleging that the companies had violated copyright law by training their AI tools on its articles without permission. Now, the government has stepped in, arguing that OpenAI’s actions were within bounds.

The letter argued that the Times’ definition of fair use is “inconsistent” with current copyright law, and that a win for the paper could have disastrous consequences. “Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility,” lawyers for the government wrote.
While the letter focuses on the New York Times and OpenAI, the government noted that its arguments apply to all of the parties in this case and related cases, including other publishers and authors.
points: The US government wrote a letter in support of OpenAI’s argument that training AI on others' intellectual property is fair use.

highlights.title: Dragon Ball Super Shares Release Date and Spectacular Trailer Full of New Details
highlights.summary: The wait is over: the remake of the Dragon Ball Super anime, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, finally has a release date. The long-awaited next entry in the Dragon Ball franchise will debut on Fuji TV on Oct. 11. Fans in the US will be able to catch a world-premiere screening of the first episode on Oct.
body: A new "super surge trailer" accompanied the announcement, giving Dragon Ball fans the first extensive look at what the remake will look like. It's safe to say that Toei Animation did not disappoint: The trailer showcases the high-quality visuals everybody expected from this remake, and also sheds light on how long the anime will be and which arcs it will cover.

The trailer also revealed the anime's opening and ending themes: "Onogami" by Megatera - Zero and "Kan Peki No Peki" by VK Blanka. While fans will miss the iconic opening theme of the original anime, "Chosetsu Dynamic!", the new songs from these young Japanese artists convey the same sense of energy and excitement, and overall contribute to giving Dragon Ball Super: Beerus a fresh vibe.

In terms of differences, fans noticed that in the trailer scenes showing Goku's battle against Frieza, the protagonist uses his Super Saiyan God form before transforming into Super Saiyan Blue, a detail that was missing from the Resurrection 'F' movie. It may not seem like much, but true Dragon Ball fans live and die for these small details, so this makes the expectations around Dragon Ball Super: Beerus even higher.

highlights.title: Rachel Roddy’s summer minestrone with pesto – recipe | A kitchen in Rome
highlights.summary: A fresh, seasonal vegetable soup that can be made in advance and only improves in texture and flavour over time. Now that I am an accomplished sourdough maker, soon to start my own micro-bakery and YouTube channel … Only joking!
body: It is a shame, then, that I didn’t give the same attention to the pan of summer minestrone I had felt so pleased with myself for cooking, cutting the courgettes carefully so they looked like Trivial Pursuit scoring wedges, while drinking tea and listening for the bottle bank lorry to drop the glass into its box, and before the sun (or anyone else) was up. Even though the combined taste of minestrone and milky Yorkshire tea is interesting, I knew it had turned out particularly well. I put on the lid, left the pan at the back of the stove and went out.

It must have been 11am by the time I got back home with a plant of basil quietly suffocating behind its plastic cone. The kitchen was already hot and the minestrone was only slightly, but unequivocally, fizzy. A spoonful of pesto did not balance it out – but please don’t let my neglect put you off making this abundantly fresh-green and creamy-white courgette, green and white bean minestrone, inspired by three recipes in Laura Ragoni’s Profumi e Sapori di Liguria.

highlights.title: These Russian Mathematicians Taught AI Models How to Talk to Each Other Without Using Words
highlights.summary: A startup called Mostik has a wild new approach to combining the capabilities of AI models.
body: I recently met with some brilliant Russian mathematicians who showed me a way for artificial intelligence models to communicate via something akin to machine telepathy.

The mathematicians work for a startup called Mostik—the Russian word for bridge. It’s a nod to the group’s approach, which allows different models to interact using the mathematical values found in their weights —the things that determine how a prompt gets turned into an output. In practice, this means the capabilities of a larger model can be fed to a smaller model to ramp up its intelligence much more efficiently.

The startup used the approach to build a model that has rocketed to the top of ARC-AGI 3, a notoriously difficult competition for AI models. (They wouldn’t tell me more because they want to win the contest.) To demonstrate the idea, however, they also created a bridge between two Chinese open-weight models: the largest version of GLM-5.2, which has 753 billion parameters; and a 4-billion-parameter version of Qwen-3.5 that can run on a mobile device. The resulting hybrid system costs one-twentieth of the full GLM model, and its performance is exactly halfway between the two.
points: A startup called Mostik has a wild new approach to combining the capabilities of AI models.

highlights.title: 11 Best MAPPA Anime That Aren’t 'Jujutsu Kaisen' or 'Chainsaw Man'
highlights.summary: It's impossible to escape the monolithic shadow of Studio MAPPA when looking at today’s anime landscape. For a majority of fans, the name is synonymous with a specific flavor of modern blockbuster.
body: Founded in 2011 by Madhouse co-founder and industry rebel Masao Maruyama, the studio was originally envisioned as an artistic sanctuary. Long before it was trusted to helm storied projects like Attack on Titan and Vinland Saga, MAPPA was built as a boutique haven where legendary directors could escape the shackles of corporate production committees and build personal passion projects that nobody else would fund. Over the years, that indie-darling DNA has collided with its rapid ascension in the industry, creating a unique identity that balances mainstream domination with a lingering desire to swing for the fences.

To truly appreciate MAPPA’s place in anime, you have to look past the cursed energy and the contracts. When you strip away its flagship projects, what’s left is a stunningly diverse lineup of historical dramas, subversive idol parodies, and bizarre passion projects that were once deemed unadaptable. From its very first jazz-infused steps to its most recent love letter to the grueling art of animation, here are the 11 best MAPPA anime that prove there’s more to the studio's soul than blockbuster adaptations.

highlights.title: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
highlights.summary: Amazon is trying to combat impersonation scams with a new feature that allows you to use its AI assistant to determine whether an email, text message, or phone call actually came from the company.
body: Alexa for Shopping can compare the message you received ‘against a record of every message Amazon has sent.’

As noted by Amazon, the assistant will only confirm that a message is real if it’s “completely certain.” An example shared by Amazon shows a customer asking, “Did Amazon just text me an OTP from 98626? Message came around 4:50pm.” Alexa for Shopping responds by confirming that Amazon actually did send the message, saying, “This was a genuine One Time Password from Amazon.”

If Alexa for Shopping determines a message isn’t from Amazon, it will instruct customers to check their orders in the app and contact Amazon’s support team directly. The company launched a similar feature earlier this year that lets you forward suspicious messages to “verify@amazon.com” to check if they’re real.
This isn’t the only recent update Amazon has launched for Alexa for Shopping, as it added an “Update Me When” feature that can now help you track new product releases as well.

highlights.title: 31 Years Later, the Smartest 'Calvin and Hobbes' Character Still Doesn't Get the Recognition They Deserve
highlights.summary: Every once in a while, some fan artist draws a continuation or sequel to Calvin and Hobbes, which is frequently themed around the idea of an adult Calvin passing Hobbes on to his own child.
body: Hobbes and Bacon is probably the best example of what's become an oddly persistent trope in Calvin and Hobbes fan lore: Calvin growing up to marry Susie. It's understandable how someone might have that reading. Susie is Calvin's only consistent peer throughout the strip's original run. If Calvin's going to marry any canon character, she's really the only option on the board. It's simultaneously a strange choice, though, as the strip usually treats Susie and Calvin like oil and water.

There are exceptions, such as the Valentine's Day arc from 1986, and that can be chalked up to the same early installment weirdness that gave us Calvin's Uncle Max. Otherwise, Susie is in Calvin and Hobbes to serve as Calvin's foil: well-adjusted vs. Calvin's maladjusted, a good student vs. a scholastic misfit, order vs. chaos. While there are occasional hints that Calvin and Susie might have a crush on one another, it's still difficult to believe they could ever stay in the same room long enough to have a civil conversation, let alone a kid.

Merge Mansion, credited with kickstarting the merge genre on mobile, retains a loyal player base. According to AppMagic estimates, the merge puzzler has generated around $7.7m in the last 30 days alone, and is thought to have earned around $540m since its 2020 launch.

highlights.title: The 2026 El Niño Is Being ‘Supersized’ as Impacts Worsen
highlights.summary: The World Meteorological Organization is warning that the climate phenomenon that has the Pacific running a fever will last until at least February, with dire consequences for weather worldwide.
body: The world’s leading weather organization is sounding the alarm about this year’s super El Niño, issuing its most certain forecast in the history of the organization.

In an update issued early Thursday, the World Meteorological Organization predicted a “nearly 100% likelihood” that the El Niño will last through February. The strong language from the World Meteorological Organization—the United Nations’ weather and climate agency—underlies just how historic this El Niño is shaping up to be.
“This is the first time that a WMO El Niño/La Niña Update has been so unequivocal,” the agency says, noting that certainty reflects “the strong agreement within WMO’s extensive network.”

El Niño is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon defined by warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures in the eastern tropical Pacific, a pattern that disrupts weather patterns around the world. Scientists have been warning since the start of the year that a particularly strong El Niño was set to develop. The latest forecasts indicate it will be the strongest on record by a wide margin, and impacts are already being felt throughout the world—and they’re likely to intensify in the coming months.

body: As usual, State of Play will be streamed live on Sony’s YouTube and Twitch channels.

The first State of Play broadcast will offer updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners. The livestream will close out with an extended look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, and immediately after, it'll be followed by a new episode of State of Play Japan. Hosted by Yuki Kaji, State of Play Japan will be focused entirely on upcoming games from game studios in Japan and Asia, so expect trailers and gameplay aplenty.

September alone is packed with new releases, including the PS5-exclusive Marvel's Wolverine alongside Control Resonant, NBA 2K27, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, so new trailers for those games wouldn't be unlikely. Looking ahead to October, there are even more high-profile releases like Hellraiser: Revival, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Final Fantasy Resonance, just to name a few. And in November?
points: As usual, State of Play will be streamed live on Sony’s YouTube and Twitch channels.
The first State of Play broadcast will offer updates and announcements from PlayStation Studios and third-party partners.
The livestream will close out with an extended look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, and immediately after, it'll be followed by a new episode of State of Play Japan.

highlights.title: Warner Music India Unveils Season 2 of Folk Music Franchise ‘Maati’ (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: Warner Music India has launched season two of “Maati,” its folk music franchise, opening on Sept. 3 with the Sufi qawwali “Jalwa-e-Jaanaan” as the eight-track season begins rolling out across eight languages.
body: Each track in the new season is tied to a specific place tied to its tradition, with the artists, communities and regional settings built into the visual presentation of the music itself.

Nooran said, “‘Jalwa-e-Jaanaan’ carries a beautiful thought that the divine and the seeker are not separate, but find meaning in each other. Singing a piece with such depth was a truly soulful experience, and I hope its emotion resonates with listeners beyond language.”

Saikia said the track’s soundscape aimed to hold the depth of Azmi’s poetry and Nooran’s voice while retaining the soul of Sufi music. “The song explores love, devotion and the pursuit of the divine, and Maati gave us the opportunity to revisit this timeless tradition through a contemporary musical lens while staying true to its essence,” he said.

“Maati” launched in October 2024 and its debut season has reached more than 78 million digitally. Season 2 widens that footprint, extending the franchise’s musical and cultural range while keeping its focus on its traditions.
points: Warner Music India has launched season two of “Maati,” its folk music franchise, opening on Sept.

highlights.title: I used to think I was an ambivalent mother, then my child started to stutter | Bridie Jabour
highlights.summary: I snapped at my children. Resented daily pickup. But I was there when he needed me, and my perception of myself completely changed. I still can’t pinpoint when it happened, but it felt as though my child lost the ability to communicate overnight.
body: Of course, that is not what happened, and he never lost the ability to communicate. But it felt as though he did at the time. And even with the benefit of hindsight, it felt like he went from a chatty three-year-old to being unable to get a sentence out. “W-w-w-w-w-w-w-w-w-what c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-can I-I-I-I-I-I-I” and then silence as he gave up trying and just looked up at me.

I often joke my parenting approach is one of benign neglect, and that I lack any instinct at all. I still do lean into that caricature at times (“I will have to do a few minutes of parenting this weekend,” I recently texted the family group chat in mock horror). This joke originated when I first became a mother more than eight years ago. I perpetuated this idea that my children were not the centre of my world and therefore I was somehow different from other mothers.
Privately I thought I was more ambivalent about motherhood than I anticipated. It turns out I had mistaken what maternal ambivalence was.
points: But I was there when he needed me, and my perception of myself completely changed.
I still can’t pinpoint when it happened, but it felt as though my child lost the ability to communicate overnight.
Of course, that is not what happened, and he never lost the ability to communicate.
